# Public-domain false-alarm set

Good human writing that must stay quiet: no hard findings, and nothing at medium or above. Every text is in the public domain (published before 1929, or a work of the US federal government). A new prose rule ships only when it stays quiet on all of these.

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `gettysburg.txt` | Abraham Lincoln, Gettysburg Address (1863), Bliss copy |
| `second-inaugural.txt` | Abraham Lincoln, Second Inaugural Address (1865), closing paragraph |
| `declaration.txt` | US Declaration of Independence (1776), second paragraph, opening |
| `constitution-preamble.txt` | US Constitution (1787), Preamble |
| `austen.txt` | Jane Austen, Pride and Prejudice (1813), chapter 1 opening |
| `walden.txt` | Henry David Thoreau, Walden (1854), "Where I Lived, and What I Lived For" |
| `dickens.txt` | Charles Dickens, A Tale of Two Cities (1859), opening sentence |
| `emancipation.txt` | Abraham Lincoln, Emancipation Proclamation (1863), opening paragraph |
